editorial:
Imagine a version of the classic puppet story that feels more like a real, gritty fairy tale than a bright cartoon. You follow a wooden boy who comes to life in Italy during a scary time of war and strict leaders. Instead of just trying to be a real boy, you see him deal with a grieving father who is struggling to stay positive. The vibe is a bit darker than the Disney version, but it has a huge heart. It feels like a handmade piece of art because the animation looks like actual puppets moving in a real world, which makes the whole experience feel special and cozy.

What really hits home is the acting and the way the story handles loss and love. You will love how the puppet is a bit of a rebel, which makes him feel like a real kid. While the political parts might feel a bit heavy for very small children, the emotional payoff is totally worth it. It is a great pick for a family movie night if you want something with more depth.
endingExplained: After a big battle, Pinocchio actually dies to save his father. However, because he was a good and selfless soul, a magical fairy brings him back to life as a real human boy. This shows that being a real boy is not about how you look, but about how you love others. He and his father get a second chance at a happy life together, finally finding peace after all the war and sadness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep stories and beautiful animation.
